Hello! That sounds like a wonderful way to celebrate. For a relaxed, scenic experience without early alarms, I recommend staying in Healdsburg or Yountville to keep drive times short.

Start your days late, enjoying a leisurely breakfast before heading out. The Silverado Trail offers stunning, quiet views between Napa and Sonoma, perfect for easy stops. Consider wineries like Mayacamas or Ridge for their beautiful settings and welcoming, unhurried atmospheres. Since you want to avoid early mornings, booking afternoon tasting slots ensures you can sleep in. Pair your visits with a nice picnic lunch at a local spot like the Farmhouse Inn or a scenic park. This approach maximizes relaxation and scenery while keeping the itinerary flexible and stress-free. Enjoy your anniversary!

Don’t forget to pack a cozy blanket for sunset views. Prioritize comfort over quantity; selecting just one or two wineries per day ensures you stay refreshed and enjoy every moment together. Have a wonderful trip!

Hello! What a lovely way to celebrate. For a relaxed, late-start journey, I highly recommend the Anderson Valley in Mendocino. The drive is stunningly scenic with fewer crowds than Napa. You can easily sleep in, then enjoy leisurely tastings at places like Navarro or Quail Hill, which offer beautiful views and a laid-back vibe. Alternatively, consider the Russian River Valley in Sonoma. It’s close to great brunch spots for a late breakfast, followed by easy stops at boutique wineries like Williams Selyem or Hirsch. Both areas allow for a slow pace, letting you savor the landscape and wine without rushing. Enjoy your anniversary!
